reviewNote: v2.0.0 sample set. Statistics copied from USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 world tables on 2026-11-17; deposit locations and products from Wikidata/Wikipedia (AI-assisted build). Every statistical question names its year. A human spot-check is recommended before wide release.

questions.text: Which country mined the most copper in 2024? Tap it on the map.
questions.explanation: Chile mined about 5.5 million tonnes of copper in 2024, nearly a quarter of the world total, ahead of DR Congo and Peru.

questions.text: Select the three countries that mined the most copper in 2024.
questions.explanation: In 2024: Chile 5.51 million t, DR Congo 2.99 million t, Peru 2.74 million t. China (1.84 million t) came fourth.

questions.text: One country mined about three-quarters of the world's cobalt in 2024. Tap it.
questions.explanation: DR Congo mined an estimated 226,000 t of cobalt in 2024, about 75% of the world total. Indonesia was a distant second.

questions.text: DR Congo mined about three-quarters of the world's supply of which metal in 2024?
questions.explanation: Cobalt. Its leading use worldwide is in lithium-ion batteries.

questions.text: Which country mined the most lithium in 2024? Tap it on the map.
questions.explanation: Australia mined an estimated 82,700 t of lithium in 2024, ahead of Chile (48,900 t) and China (41,400 t).

questions.text: Production, reserves and resources are not the same thing. Match each lithium statistic with the country that leads it.
questions.description: Mine production: what was dug up in one year. Reserves: what can be mined profitably today. Resources: everything identified in the ground.
questions.explanation: Australia mines the most lithium, Chile has the largest reserves (9.2 million t) and Argentina the largest identified resources (28 million t), according to USGS.

questions.text: True or false: Australia mined the most lithium in 2024, but Chile has the largest lithium reserves.
questions.explanation: True. Australia led 2024 mine production, while Chile's reserves (9.2 million t) are larger than Australia's (8.4 million t).

questions.text: Which country mined the most gold in 2024?
questions.explanation: China mined 377 t of gold in 2024, ahead of Russia (about 310 t) and Australia (284 t).

questions.text: According to USGS, which country has the largest gold reserves?
questions.explanation: Australia, with about 13,000 t, just ahead of Russia (12,000 t). China mines the most gold but has smaller reserves.

questions.text: Which country mined the most iron ore in 2024? Tap it on the map.
questions.explanation: Australia produced about 982 million t of usable iron ore in 2024, more than twice as much as Brazil.

questions.text: Which country mined the most nickel in 2024?
questions.explanation: Indonesia mined about 2.31 million t of nickel in 2024, more than half of the world total.

questions.text: Which country mined the most rare earths in 2024?
questions.explanation: China, with an estimated 270,000 t of rare-earth oxide in 2024, about 70% of the world total. The United States was second.

questions.text: What is mined at the marked mine in northern Sweden?
questions.explanation: The Kiruna mine in Swedish Lapland is an iron ore mine.

questions.text: The marked mine in Botswana is the richest mine of its kind in the world. What does it produce?
questions.explanation: Jwaneng in Botswana is the richest diamond mine in the world.

questions.text: So much of one metal has come out of the marked region in South Africa that the country's currency, the rand, is named after it. Which metal?
questions.explanation: Gold. The rand, introduced in 1961, takes its name from the Witwatersrand.

questions.text: This salt flat in Chile is a major source of which metal, extracted from its brines?
questions.explanation: Lithium. Since the 2000s the Salar de Atacama has become a major hub for extracting lithium from its brines.

questions.text: Ghawar, the largest conventional oil field in the world, is in which country? Tap it.
questions.explanation: Ghawar is in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, about 280 km long.

questions.text: The Mir mine was the Soviet Union's first developed diamond mine. In which country is it today? Tap it.
questions.explanation: The Mir mine is in Mirny, in Russia's Sakha Republic in eastern Siberia.

questions.text: The Grasberg mine holds one of the largest gold and copper reserves in the world. Tap the country where it is.
questions.explanation: Grasberg is in Indonesia, in the Indonesian part of the island of New Guinea.

questions.text: Match each mine with its country.
questions.explanation: Escondida (copper) is in Chile's Atacama Desert, Kiruna (iron ore) in Sweden, Jwaneng (diamonds) in Botswana and Grasberg (gold and copper) in Indonesia.
